key_insight: Using only three sensors, the method combines phase-amplitude reduction with machine learning to design optimal actuation that rapidly synchronizes airfoil wake shedding while controlling lift fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical control strategy for post-stall airfoils that can speed up flow-state changes without introducing large aerodynamic unsteadiness, which is important for aeroelastic safety and performance.
method: Reconstruct the wake state from sparse sensor measurements with a nonlinear machine-learning model.
Derive time-varying phase and amplitude sensitivity fields to locate and time the most effective forcing.
Compute an amplitude-penalized optimal waveform for fast synchronization under lift-fluctuation constraints.
evidence_signal: The approach was tested on flows over multiple NACA airfoils at several post-stall angles of attack, where the optimized forcing changed wake frequency faster than standard sinusoidal actuation and reduced lift-coefficient fluctuations by 20% with amplitude penalty.
watch_item: The method depends on accurate sparse sensing and model-based sensitivity fields, so robustness to noise, changing flow regimes, and real-time implementation limits should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Machine-learning-assisted phase-amplitude reduction for fast synchronization of airfoil wakes with constrained fluctuations
